notices.short_title: Capacity Building MWBE for Cultivating Partnerships Renewal
notices.description: This solicitation is being made pursuant to the M/WBE Noncompetitive Small Purchase Method, Section 3-08 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, this procurement is exclusively for the City Certified Minority and Woman Owned Business (M/WBEs). Contracts awarded under this method may not exceed $500,000, inclusive of any and all change orders, overruns, amendments, renewals and extensions. Through this solicitation, The Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD) is seeking an appropriately qualified vendor to support small and emerging community-based organizations, including faith-based organizations, to better serve their communities through networking with other community leaders and established organizations, and provide connections to consultants and mentoring institutions as appropriate.

To support CBOs in a variety of activities focused on structuring organizational policies and practices to promote anti-racism and build and enhance approaches to equity. Examples may include developing their own equity statements, conducting internal reviews, developing accommodations/policies for serving participants with disabilities, and supporting the development and implementation of processes to reevaluate CBO's existing policies and practices.

This solicitation is being made pursuant to the M/WBE Noncompetitive Small Purchase Method, Section 3-08 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, this procurement is exclusively for the City Certified Minority and Woman Owned Business (M/WBEs). Contracts awarded under this method may not exceed $500,000, inclusive of any and all change orders, overruns, amendments, renewals and extensions.

notices.short_title: COMPASS Center Based - Bronx 02, 05, Mn 10, & Qn 12 Middle
notices.description: COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs. Awarded for COMPASS Center-Based - Bronx -CD 2 -991 Longwood Avenue, Bronx, NY 10459, Bronx CD-5 - 2255 Webster Avenue, Bronx, NY 10457 - Manhattan CD-10 - 441 Manhattan Avenue, New York, NY 10026 - Queens CD-12 -116-25 Guy R Brewer Boulvard Queens, NY 11434

notices.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notices.description:
Notice of Concept Paper

The NYC Department of Social Service (DSS)/Human Resources Administration (HRA) is committed to strengthening and modernizing the NYCBenefits Program to promote accountability, workforce capacity, cross-system coordination, and high-quality, client-centered services. The purpose of this document is to:
 

  1. Outline HRAs proposed enhancements to the NYCBenefits service model;
  2. Solicit stakeholder feedback regarding program design and operational requirements;
  3. Assess provider interest and organizational capacity; and
  4. Inform the development of a Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx.

Anticipated number of contracts: Between thirty-eight (38) and fifty-eight (58), aligned with the following provider specializations:
 

  • Thirty-five (35) to fifty-three (53) Direct service vendors
  • Three (3) to five (5) Technical Assistance vendors


Anticipated annual funding: $9,750,0000 to $14,950,000 over the three (3) year contract term (approximately $300-$350 per client), subject to funding availability.
